# Flow: two-stage load (export parts, then build)

One-line summary: stage 1 keeps every Snowflake read as a Parquet part in `.cache/reads/<key>/`, so a load that stops resumes with only the missing parts; stage 2 builds the role graph, the rules and the copies from those parts without Snowflake (`cache.py:320-324`, README.md:164).

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant R as run.py / page
    participant S as server.py
    participant P as cache.parted (parts)
    participant A as access.py (snapshot / live / each)
    participant SF as Snowflake
    participant C as cache.store
    R->>S: first page (load_shared) or run.py --export
    S->>S: tracked(KEY, "shared", stages)
    S->>A: with_query(fn, KEY): query = parted(query, KEY, OFFLINE)
    A->>P: each(query, sqls, what) -> query.keep(sqls, what, run)
    P->>P: take(name): part kept and ok? rows from parquet
    P->>SF: only the missing / timed-out parts (one login, at the first statement)
    SF-->>P: rows -> write_part + parts.json
    P-->>A: rows per statement (or the kept exception)
    A-->>S: snapshot / live dict
    S->>C: cache.get -> store: memory, .pkl, SQL copy thread
    S->>S: built(d): a.step build, rule checks, fixes (ro, breaks), save (or kept_rules), sens
    S-->>R: pages answer; "Ready in N s"
```

## Steps

1. `run.py --export [--fresh]` starts `python server.py --export` (`run.py:44-45`); `server.export(fresh)` clears the parts on `--fresh`, reads the shared data with progress lines on the terminal, builds nothing, prints the parts and the timed-out ones; all ok -> `cache.drop(KEY)` so the next start builds from the new parts, exit 0; else 1 — `server.py:3489-3512`, `server.py:3517-3518`.
2. A page load: `load_shared()` answers from memory / `.pkl` at once; Direct mode with no copy and no parts needs the click (409 `shared_not_loaded`); a load already running answers 409 `shared_loading` (the page never waits) — `server.py:208-227`. Else `tracked(KEY, "shared", stages)` — `server.py:221`.
3. `stages()`: stage 1 `cache.get(KEY, read_shared)`, stage 2 `built(d)`, then "Ready in N s" — `server.py:179-186`.
4. `read_shared(key)`: Direct mode starts from `cache.old(key, KEY)` (the earlier ACTIVITY / OBJECT_USE rows, kept as `old.pkl` with the parts, so a resumed load asks for the same days and its part names stay the same) — `server.py:161-169`, `cache.py:349-364`; objects mode passes `old=cache.last(KEY)` and `snapshot()` asks the last OK run through `query.fresh` on every load (never answered from a part), so a newer run shows and an unchanged one reads no table again — `server.py:169`, `access.py:522-524`, `cache.py:578-579`.
5. `with_query(fn, key)`: the connection is made at the first statement that goes to Snowflake (one login across `each()`'s threads; a failed login fails every statement as `ConnectionError`), so a load answered from parts logs in to nothing; `query` is wrapped by `cache.parted(query, key, OFFLINE)` when disk is allowed; a statement that lost the session (`a.lost`: also error 606, no warehouse) is remembered and raised after `fn` returns, since `live()` and `mine()` turn a failed read into an empty table; a whole load then calls `q.prune()`, which drops the parts it did not ask for (an older run's tables, older activity days) — `server.py:90-127`, `server.py:118-124`, `cache.py:506-514`.
6. `each()` hands a wave to `query.keep(sqls, what, run)` — `access.py:719-721`. `keep()`: heavy reads (a list of names) are a part each, kept the moment each answers; a wave of like statements is one part, and a wave whose statements timed out reads only those again (`cache.py:563-574`) — `cache.py:549-576`. Single statements go through `q(sql)` — `cache.py:538-547`.
7. Part names: label + sha1 of the statements (`part_name`, `cache.py:431-434`): another run or other days is another part. `take()` reads a kept part unless it failed (a timeout), a single statement's rows as written (no copy), else rows rebuilt per statement from `__i` and the kept errors — `cache.py:445-464`. `put()` writes `<name>.parquet` with every column any statement of the wave answered and the `parts.json` entry (`save()`, `.tmp` then rename); a lost session or an offline build is never kept; without pyarrow or duckdb nothing is kept (one load-log line); a part of mixed types stays in memory only — `cache.py:466-504`. The engine is `pyarrow.parquet` when it imports, else DuckDB (`COPY ... (FORMAT parquet)`, one typed list per column, `duck_type`), else none — `cache.py:367-376`, `cache.py:379-428`.
8. A `USE` answered from its part is replayed before the next statement that goes to Snowflake — `cache.py:516-525`, `cache.py:543-544`.
9. `cache.get` -> `store(key, d)`: memory; `.pkl` (previous kept as `.prev.pkl`); the SQL copy in a `COPYING` thread; a read with no OK run stays in memory only — `cache.py:123-162`.
10. `built(d)`: under `LOCK`, `a.step("Building the role graph")` `a.build`, a count line; unless `kept_rules()` put the results back: `a.step("Checking the rules")` `a.rule_rows`, with findings `a.step("Working out what each fix changes")` (rule 17 `a.readonly_writes` as `ro` when `HIERARCHY_ON`, `breaks(rows, ro)`), `a.step("Saving the rule results")` `kept_rules(save=True)`; then `a.step("Preparing the pages")` `a.sensitive` as `sens`. The first page's `session()` finds all of it in `a.memo`, so a page after "Ready" does not sit on Loading — `server.py:189-205`, `server.py:349-371`, `server.py:333-338`.
11. `run.py --build` sets `BUILD_ONLY=1` (`run.py:46-47`): `OFFLINE` (`server.py:28`) makes `parted(..., offline=True)` fail a missing part as "not exported yet (python run.py --export reads it)" and never connect — `cache.py:517-518`; refreshes answer `BUILD_ONLY_NOTE` — `server.py:3151-3152`.
12. Parts are read again only on Rebuild snapshot / Read Snowflake again ([background-refresh.md](background-refresh.md)), a fresh My access load (`server.py:295`) or `--export --fresh`; "Data from" shows the oldest part's time (`fetched`, `server.py:236-239`, `cache.py:344-346`).

Test: `test_server.test_built_ready` — `server.built(a.fake())` under `a.progress` leaves `rows`, `ro`, `breaks` and `sens` in `a.memo` and logs "Working out what each fix changes" and "Preparing the pages" — test_server.py:1142-1154.

## Example (test_server.test_parts, fake connection)

- A first load keeps every read as a part; one part marked timed out -> the next load reads only that statement.
- `BUILD_ONLY=1` reads nothing from Snowflake; `--export --fresh` reads every part again; `run.command(["--export", "--fresh"])` -> `python server.py --export --fresh`, `--build` -> `BUILD_ONLY=1` — `test_server.py:1207-1259`.

## Unclear

- Parts have no age limit: data from an old export stays until a manual refresh or `--export --fresh` (`cache.py:320-324`); "Data from" shows its time (inferred: by design, README.md:164).

Rule: [business_rule:read_parts](../logic/rules.md). Data: [data/duckdb-copy.md](../data/duckdb-copy.md).
